title: Unit: access, shared devices, and your active crew
audience: Crews using an apparatus tablet, vehicle device, or shared operational workstation.
summary: Sign in as an accountable person, select the correct apparatus, organize its crew, and understand shared-session and security controls.
prerequisites: A training member assigned to the station group that owns a demonstration unit; configured roles and unit statuses.
A shared-session policy and verification methods for the optional shared-device branch.
SSO, passkeys, and MFA only where actually configured; native hardware for operating-system permission captures.

Preserve Engine51 unit role51001 Officer/TeamLead = Christopher Herrmann only. The other five units remain unassigned; do not change member status, shift assignments or qualifications for this crew example.

scenes.title: Understand the person and the apparatus
scenes.capture_intent: Show authenticated member identity and active-unit context; open Settings. Use actual application screenshots and observed controls; source support alone is not capture proof.
scenes.narration: Unit follows the apparatus context selected on this device, while a named person signs in. Identify both before working. The active unit scopes status, roles, map context, routes, and inventory; review it in Settings at each handoff. This is useful for a SAR vehicle, community response team, or industrial standby. A vehicle-mounted tablet still needs the correct member and apparatus selection.
scenes.practice: Identify the signed-in training member and the apparatus the tablet is intended to represent before changing any operational data.

source_workflow_reference.title: Understand the person and the apparatus
source_workflow_reference.narration: Unit follows the apparatus or crew context selected on this device, while a person still signs in with their own account. Start by identifying both. The active unit determines relevant status, roles, map context, routes, and inventory. Settings is where you review that selection. A tablet mounted in a vehicle does not remove individual accountability, and it does not automatically select the right apparatus for today’s crew.

scenes.title: Configure a shared installation deliberately
scenes.capture_intent: Open Shared device setup and show toggle/label/Save; if configuration is changed, verify normal next sign-in rather than injecting session state. Use actual application screenshots and observed controls; source support alone is not capture proof.

It identifies the installation; it does not turn a person’s credentials into a shared crew password. Each member still follows the department’s session and verification policy.

source_workflow_reference.title: Practice lock and shift handoff
source_workflow_reference.narration: After a supported Shared device sign-in, inspect the session bar and its Lock control. Idle or background behavior follows policy; Stay signed in may appear near an idle deadline. Unlock with the verification method permitted for the current member, or use End shift and Switch operator for a handoff. Check the resulting account and session state before resuming work. Enabling a setup toggle differs from verifying the device’s actual lock behavior.

scenes.title: Select the apparatus you actually have
scenes.capture_intent: Open Active Unit/Select Unit and choose authorized Engine51; verify Current Unit. Use actual application screenshots and observed controls; source support alone is not capture proof.
scenes.narration: In Settings, open Active Unit and choose the apparatus for this crew. Select Unit lists the units accessible to this member, and Current Unit helps confirm the result. The selection scopes several operational screens and should be checked at every handoff.

source_workflow_reference.title: Assign the actual crew roles

Review the assignments again after a crew change so the displayed resource picture remains useful.

scenes.title: Read the unit status before changing it
scenes.capture_intent: Use actual sidebar/header, ordinary quick-status steps and Set Active status selector. Do not imply the read-only status card is an entry button or invent a literal Current status label. Hold/restriction variants remain conditional.
scenes.narration: The sidebar shows the active unit’s state. A quick status button opens that status’s destination or note steps; Set Active also opens Select Status. This department uses ordinary Submit. Two-second holding and next-status restrictions depend on configuration. Read the offered destinations and note before submitting, then confirm the saved unit state. Unit status remains separate from the operator’s personal staffing.
scenes.practice: Compare the active apparatus status with a member’s personal availability, then choose a valid training status transition.

source_workflow_reference.title: Read the unit status before changing it
source_workflow_reference.narration: The status controls represent the active unit. Read Current and inspect the next options allowed by its workflow. Press and hold a quick status for two seconds when you intend to change it. Show all statuses reveals additional choices; Show next statuses only restores the guided sequence. Your personal staffing availability belongs in Responder, so explain which identity this status change will affect before applying it.

scenes.capture_intent: Use reviewed actual Unit screens for the available controls in this scene. Preserve the stated unexercised/provider/shared-session limits; never substitute error overlays or an installation label for operational lock/unlock proof.
scenes.narration: The call card shows the selected incident. View Call Details opens its full screen. Directions offers a mapping handoff, which is unexercised here. Deselect concerns app selection; incident closure is separate. Set Active selected our practice incident and opened Select Status. The unit’s response changed only after the status submission, so verify selection and response separately before describing the crew as dispatched or responding.

source_workflow_reference.title: Understand the sidebar incident context
source_workflow_reference.narration: The call card connects the active unit’s workspace to an incident. Select Active Call chooses from available calls; View Call Details opens the full incident information. Directions hands off to the supported mapping application, and Deselect clears the current selection through its confirmation. Selecting a call is different from changing the unit’s response status, so inspect both before describing the crew as dispatched, en route, or available.

scenes.title: Keep account security and recovery visible

This lesson inspects configuration and recovery prerequisites without enrolling a method, replacing an authenticator, or changing credentials. Login Info and Logout help with handoff; verify the actual account and session after a normal sign-in or sign-out.

source_workflow_reference.title: Keep account security and recovery visible
source_workflow_reference.narration: Settings provides Sign-in and security for the person using Unit. Review the authenticator state, passkeys, and Recent verifications. Add a passkey only for an authorized account and supported platform. Login info helps confirm identity, and Logout supports a clean handoff. Lost-factor recovery can replace an authenticator and end sessions, so practice on a disposable account. Responder approval is a separate flow whose result should be checked on the requesting device.
